page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text with a catchword at the foot; no margin notes.

main_text.p: ut impraesens disputemus; uti nec de foris Ecclesiasticis, quot, aut quibus, certe non citra necessitatem multiplicandis. Scripta super Controversiis Dissentientium fratrum, quos vulgo Independentes vocant, extant varia, quaeque ad manus nostras venere praecipua quidem, Syons prerogative Royal, ostendens quod quaelibet particularis Congregatio est independens; is an independant body, not standing under any other ecclesiasticall authoritie out of it selfe. Independentium, qui sic appellantur, Apologia, cum Antapologia Thomae Edwardi, qua illam refutavit. Rationes per Dissentientes fratres oblatae adversus Propositiones concernentes Regimen Presbyteriale, cum Responsionibus Synodi ad illas, Anglice: ubi disputatur de rebus in controversia. Papers for accommodation anno MDCXLIV. in quibus de componendis, aut uniendis, vel tolerandis dissensionibus & dissentientibus hinc inde actum. A survey of the summe of Church discipline, duobus libris, quorum primum scripsit Tho. Hooker; alterum Joh. Cotton, pro ordine Ecclesiarum Congregationalium in Nova Anglia. Adversus illos Rob. Baylie, lib. a Dissuasive from the Errours of the time, ch. III. IV. V. VI. X. Jus divinum Regiminis Ecclesiastici, pro Regimine presbyteriali, per Ministros Londinenses, Anglice. A vindication of the Presbyteriall government, per Ministros Synodi Provincialis Londinensis a. MDCXLIX. Sam. Rutherfurd, lib. The due right of presbyteries: aliique ejusdem tractatus. Joh. Paget, A defence of Church government, adversus Ainsworthum, Davenportium, & Cannum, de potestate presbyterii, Classium, & Synodorum. Samuel Bolton, The Arraignement of Errour, a pag. 268. &c. imprimis a pag. 349. ubi de compositione controversiarum egregie disserit. Cui fini facit etiam Iohn Brinsley, The Arraignement of the present Schisme of new separation in Old England: Ex Nostris, Vocius, Disp. de Classibus, & Synodis. De Ecclesia

page.notes: Text is in a mixture of roman and italic; the Greek-free page has no marginal notes. Some words are blurred by print quality and may be misread, notably "Vocius" (possibly Voetius), "Syons" and the roman numerals in the date "MDCXLIV" and "MDCXLIX", which appear as "clɔ Iɔ c xliv" and "clɔ Iɔ c xlix" in the scan. Printed "Ddd 2" signature and the catchword "slesia" are as printed.
